chunks: And by this chain of transmission, from Ṣāliḥ ibn ʿUqbah, from Yazīd ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

When Fāṭimah عليها السلام was born, Allah revealed to an angel, and caused the tongue of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله to speak by it, so he named her Fāṭimah. Then He said: “Indeed, I have set you apart through knowledge, and I have set you apart from menstruation.”
Then Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: “By Allah, Allah had indeed set her apart through knowledge and from menstruation in the Covenant.”

key_terms.أَوْحَى: revealed or inspired, indicating divine communication from Allah
key_terms.الطَّمْثِ: menstruation, mentioned here in the sense of being kept apart from it
key_terms.الْمِيثَاقِ: the Covenant, referring to a pre-temporal divine covenant
key_terms.بِالْعِلْمِ: through knowledge, meaning a divinely granted distinction of knowledge
key_terms.فَاطِمَةُ: Fāṭimah, the blessed daughter of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, whose name is explained in the narration

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about why Fāṭimah عليها السلام was named Fāṭimah?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the naming of Fāṭimah عليها السلام as a divinely guided event and links her name to being specially set apart. It emphasizes her God-given knowledge and purity, presenting her distinction as established by Allah from the primordial Covenant.
